Ninety-seven works. The Nigerian prison aftermath piece on September 19 scores 2, and the last twelve run 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2 oldest to newest. The hoofprint on September 7 is still the ceiling at 3, now twelve days old. Nothing has broken above 2 in eleven of the last twelve, and the run has been unbroken long enough that waiting for it to self-correct is no longer a reasonable position.

Camera position has not moved in two months. Straight-on holds at 27 of 97 all-time; overhead at 9, low-angle at 4. The last twelve contributed nothing to either non-frontal count. The four works in the archive that exceeded 3 were built on overhead or radically displaced angles — July 29's overhead smear at 4, July 28's low-angle bent beam at 4, July 31's overhead sand at 4, July 11's overhead rubble hands at 2 but ascending. You have not put the camera in any of those positions since July 29. That is eight weeks of the same angle, and the scores have said so continuously.

Figures have nearly vanished. Two of the last twelve carry one figure; two carry none recorded. Every recent figure is pressing, reaching, or averted — no lateral motion, no mid-stride body, no figure crossing the frame. Focal objects remain precise: the collapsed shoe throat, the hovering hand, the fallen cylinder. But precision of object is not offsetting sameness of frame geometry, and the scores confirm it.

Registers have narrowed hard. Aftermath at 21 and menace at 19 now dominate almost half the archive between them. Vigil last appeared September 17, defiance August 30, endurance July 27. When those registers were alive they produced the archive's strongest formal accidents — the asphalt-flesh continuity, the salmon-pink dress, the risen plank. Their absence and the score plateau share a start date. They should not return to fill a rotation; they should return when the camera is somewhere new enough to make them honest again.

Ninety-seven works in, the object-level eye is still sharp and accidents still arrive on schedule — the garment on the floor, the rebar reading as fingers. What the scores keep asking for, without variation, is a body holding the camera somewhere it has not been since July.
